newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China likely bought South American soymeal-traders.
newsitem.headline: China likely bought South American soymeal-traders.

text.p: Hong Kong grains traders said on Wednesday China had likely bought a large quantity of soybean meal, since the price levels were suitable for Chinese buyers.
But the traders could offer no details on the deals.
"Some state-owned buyers have bought meal, maybe on Friday," said one grains trader.
Chicago Board of Trade(CBOT) May soymeal ended $0.70 down at $275.00 on Tuesday on talk China bought two to three cargoes of South American supplies.
"It makes sense to buy meal for May/June shipment and June/July arrival," another grains source said.
For forward delivery, South American meal cost US$318-320 per tonne, C&F China, traders said.
"People are bullish soymeal in China, they think the international prices will go up," said one Hong Kong source.
One trader said he heard China had purchased between 200,000 tonnes and 300,000 tonnes of soymeal, but this could not be confirmed.

Argentinian meal in China was currently around 2,740 yuan to 2,750 yuan ($330-331) per tonne, while Brazilian meal was currently priced at about 2,780 yuan per tonne, a China-based grains source noted.
